subproblem.title: Step 8: an extremal invariant member has singular set equal to its invariance subspace
subproblem.statement: Let P, n, Q ∈ ℕ, F and sing satisfy (H0), (H1), A.1, A.2, A.3c, A.3(2) and A.3(3) as in the parent theorem. Let d ∈ ℕ be such that every L-invariant ψ ∈ F (ψ(y + λx) = ψ(x) for y ∈ L, λ > 0, x) with sing ψ ≠ ∅ has dim L ≤ d. If φ ∈ F is L-invariant for a d-dimensional linear subspace L and sing φ ≠ ∅, then sing φ = L.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n Q : ℕ) (F : Set (Euclid P → Euclid Q)) (sing : (Euclid P → Euclid Q) → Set (Euclid P)), (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ ψ ∈ F, (∀ᵐ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)], φ x = ψ x) → φ = ψ) → (∀ φ ∈ F, LocallyIntegrable φ μH[(n : ℝ)]) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ (y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → lam < 1 → ‖y‖ ≤ 1 - lam → (fun x => φ (y + lam • x)) ∈ F) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ y : Euclid P, ‖y‖ < 1 → ∀ lams : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ k, 0 < lams k) → StrictAnti lams → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ (sub : ℕ → ℕ) (ψ : Euclid P → Euclid Q), StrictMono sub ∧ ψ ∈ F ∧ (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • φ (y + lams (sub k) • x) ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • ψ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) ∧ ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ x, ψ (lam • x) = ψ x) → (∀ φ ∈ F, IsClosed (sing φ)) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ (y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → lam < 1 → ‖y‖ ≤ 1 - lam → sing (fun x => φ (y + lam • x)) = (fun x => y + lam • x) ⁻¹' sing φ) → (∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ φs : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid Q, (∀ k, φs k ∈ F) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, f x • φs k x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x • φ x ∂μH[(n : ℝ)]))) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, ball (0 : Euclid P) 1 ∩ sing (φs k) ⊆ {x | ∃ z ∈ sing φ, dist x z < ε}) → ∀ d : ℕ, (∀ ψ ∈ F, ∀ L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), (∀ y ∈ L, ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ x, ψ (y + lam • x) = ψ x) → (sing ψ).Nonempty → Module.finrank ℝ L ≤ d) → ∀ φ ∈ F, ∀ L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ L = d → (∀ y ∈ L, ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ x, φ (y + lam • x) = φ x) → (sing φ).Nonempty → sing φ = (L : Set (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, proof of A.4, chapter-A.txt lines 133–139 ('sing ψ ⊇ T by A.3(2) … if there is x̃ ∈ sing ψ ∖ T … contradicting the definition of d. Therefore sing ψ = T'). This is step 8 of the parent proof.
1. For y ∈ L and λ > 0, L-invariance gives φ_{y,λ} = φ. So (A.3(2)) gives sing φ = {x : y + λx ∈ sing φ} whenever y ∈ L, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ, and sing φ is closed (A.3c). The sibling lemma adr_affine_invariant_closed_set with S := sing φ yields (i) y + λz ∈ sing φ ⇔ z ∈ sing φ for all y ∈ L, λ > 0 and z; and (ii) L ⊆ sing φ, since sing φ ≠ ∅.
2. Suppose some z ∈ sing φ ∖ L. Then z ≠ 0, since 0 ∈ L. Put x := z/(2|z|). By (i) with y = 0 and λ = 1/(2|z|), x ∈ sing φ. Also |x| = 1/2, and x ∉ L, since otherwise z = 2|z|x ∈ L.
3. Let Λ_k := (1/2)/(k + 2). This is a strictly decreasing positive sequence with Λ_k → 0 and Λ_k ≤ 1/4. (A.2) with y = x (|x| < 1) gives a strictly increasing sub and ψ ∈ F, homogeneous of degree zero, with φ_{x,λ_k} ⇀ ψ, where λ_k := Λ_{sub(k)}. Here 0 < λ_k ≤ 1/4 < 1, |x| = 1/2 ≤ 1 − λ_k and λ_k → 0.
4. By (A.1), φ_k := φ_{x,λ_k} ∈ F. By (A.3(2)), 0 ∈ sing φ_k because x + λ_k·0 = x ∈ sing φ, and 0 ∈ B_1(0). The sibling lemma adr_sing_mem_of_tendsto with z_k := 0 → 0 gives 0 ∈ sing ψ, so sing ψ ≠ ∅.
5. The sibling lemma adr_tangent_invariance with S := L shows that ψ is (L + ℝx)-invariant, and dim(L + ℝx) = d + 1 because x ∉ L. The hypothesis on d then gives d + 1 ≤ d, a contradiction. Hence sing φ ⊆ L, and with (ii), sing φ = L. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma S (sibling) gives L ⊆ sing φ and invariance of sing φ under y+λ·, y∈L, λ>0
a singular point outside L rescales to x ∈ sing φ with |x| = 1/2 and x ∉ L
A.2 at x gives a homogeneous tangent function ψ; Lemma T (sibling) gives 0 ∈ sing ψ
Lemma I (sibling) makes ψ invariant under the (d+1)-dimensional space L+ℝx, contradicting maximality of d; so sing φ = L
